title: NORVASC (amlodipine besylate) tablets for oral administration: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, NDA 019787 supplement 062, label revised October 2017
result: Indications: hypertension, chronic stable angina, vasospastic angina, and angiographically documented coronary artery disease without heart failure or an ejection fraction below 40%. Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, primarily strokes and myocardial infarctions, and the absolute risk increase per mm Hg is greater at higher blood pressures. Mechanism: a dihydropyridine calcium antagonist that inhibits the transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle, selectively and with a greater effect on vascular smooth muscle than on cardiac muscle; within the physiological pH range it is ionised (pKa 8.6) and its kinetic interaction with the calcium channel receptor is characterised by a gradual rate of association and dissociation, resulting in a gradual onset of effect; a peripheral arterial vasodilator that reduces peripheral vascular resistance; serum calcium concentration is not affected; sinoatrial nodal function and atrioventricular conduction are not changed. Dose: 5 mg once daily initially and 10 mg once daily at most; 2.5 mg once daily in small, fragile or elderly patients or in hepatic insufficiency; 7 to 14 days between titration steps. Pharmacokinetics: peak plasma concentrations 6 to 12 hours after a dose; absolute bioavailability 64 to 90%, unaltered by food; about 93% bound to plasma proteins; about 90% converted to inactive metabolites by hepatic metabolism, with 10% of the parent compound and 60% of the metabolites excreted in urine; terminal elimination half-life about 30 to 50 hours; steady state after 7 to 8 days of daily dosing; kinetics not significantly influenced by renal impairment; AUC about 40 to 60% higher in elderly patients, in hepatic insufficiency and in moderate to severe heart failure; half-life 56 hours with impaired hepatic function. Effect: in 15 double-blind placebo-controlled randomised studies in 800 patients on amlodipine and 538 on placebo, placebo-corrected reductions 24 hours after the dose averaged 12/6 mm Hg standing and 13/7 mm Hg supine in mild to moderate hypertension, with little difference between peak and trough. Oedema was dose related: 1.8% at 2.5 mg (n=275), 3.0% at 5 mg (n=296) and 10.8% at 10 mg (n=268) against 0.6% with placebo (n=520); oedema occurred in 14.6% of 512 women and 5.6% of 1218 men on amlodipine against 5.1% and 1.4% on placebo; discontinuation for adverse reactions about 1.5% against about 1% with placebo. Warnings: symptomatic hypotension is possible, particularly with severe aortic stenosis; worsening angina and acute myocardial infarction can develop after starting or increasing the dose, particularly with severe obstructive coronary artery disease. Interactions: diltiazem 180 mg daily raised amlodipine exposure by 60% in elderly hypertensive patients, and strong CYP3A inhibitors such as itraconazole and clarithromycin may raise plasma concentrations further, while cimetidine, antacids, sildenafil and grapefruit juice have no impact; amlodipine is a weak CYP3A inhibitor and 10 mg raised exposure to 80 mg simvastatin by 77%, so simvastatin is limited to 20 mg daily; trough cyclosporine rose by an average of 40% in 11 renal transplant recipients; tacrolimus exposure rose 2.5-fold to 4-fold in 9 healthy CYP3A5 expressers and did not change in 6 non-expressers. In the CAMELOT trial of 1318 patients with coronary artery disease followed for a mean 19 months, first events of the composite endpoint occurred in 110 of 663 (16.6%) on amlodipine against 151 of 655 (23.1%) on placebo, hazard ratio 0.691 (95% CI 0.540 to 0.884, p=0.003), driven by hospitalisation for angina (51, 7.7% against 84, 12.8%) and coronary revascularisation (78, 11.8% against 103, 15.7%).
